subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a durable owner-confirmed responsibility lifecycle for memory/evidence reuse, and should that contract live in core memory, plugin APIs, or an external ClawHub/plugin integration?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but selecting the owner boundary affects security posture, public plugin contracts, memory schema, UX, and compatibility in ways automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Keep as design umbrella
options.body: Use this issue to choose the security/product contract first, then split implementation into smaller memory, plugin API, UI, and audit PRs.

options.title: Limit to plugin API
options.body: Define only the missing plugin extension points and leave responsibility-chain policy to external plugins or ClawHub integrations.

options.title: Close as external workflow
options.body: Decline core changes if maintainers decide SCBKR/UMP-style responsibility chains should remain outside OpenClaw's supported product boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep as design umbrella
recommendation.body: Use this issue to choose the security/product contract first, then split implementation into smaller memory, plugin API, UI, and audit PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The most central current boundary is the memory host/plugin seam, and the verified history ties this person to that seam's extraction and provider refactors.
